summary: Practise sustainable tender design, bid evaluation and contract monitoring while protecting value for money. Explore the course and its applied tools.
lede: Sustainable public procurement brings environmental and social considerations into purchasing decisions while keeping value-for-money reasoning visible. It is for procurement officers, contract managers and project teams who need to carry requirements from planning through supplier monitoring. Using ISO 20400 guidance and procurement-cycle exercises, participants practise impact screening, life-cycle cost comparisons, proportionate tender criteria, evidence-based bid scoring and supplier KPI monitoring.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who shape or assess tenders and need to carry environmental and social requirements from planning into supplier performance monitoring.
prerequisites: Prior exposure to procurement planning, tender evaluation or contract administration is expected. No coding or programming is required. Participants should be able to work with procurement documents and basic spreadsheet calculations; advanced life-cycle costing and financing-specific procurement requirements are covered at an operational application level, with procedures adapted to the applicable project framework.
topics: Procurement for World Bank and donor-financed projects
